purpose: Skeleton-first sternum audit. Test the a003 jugular-notch to xiphisternal sternum reference against independent adult male manubrium + sternal-body morphometry.

current_a003.head_definition: jugular notch / superior manubrial reference, inset from skin
current_a003.tail_definition: xiphisternal region, inset from skin; xiphoid itself not included

conservative_sample_check.warning: The two maxima need not come from the same person. Their sum is used only as a conservative ceiling for the reported Greek sample, not as a population limit.

findings: The a003 sternum reference runs from the jugular notch to the xiphisternal region, so the closest comparison is manubrium length + sternal-body length; xiphoid length should not be added.
Across three modern CT studies, male manubrium+body mean sums are about 152-159 mm, while the a003 vertical component is ~203 mm and the 3D chord is ~213 mm.

Even the sum of the separate maximum manubrium and body lengths reported in the Greek male sample is 192 mm, below the a003 vertical component. This is a conservative sample-level warning, not a universal maximum.
The current sternum was placed from old mesh surface landmarks, so the discrepancy is consistent with the broader finding that the torso/shoulder mesh drove skeletal proportions.

Exact canonical sternum length is NOT frozen from these unconditioned population means. The final target must preserve the character's 1.82 m stature and be reconciled with thoracic vertebral levels, rib attachments, jugular notch and xiphisternal level.
canonical_actions: Represent manubrium and sternal body landmark regions separately while retaining one conventional adult sternum bone in the 206 count.
Define jugular notch, bilateral clavicular notches/SC contacts, sternal angle, costal notch levels and xiphisternal junction in a thoracic frame.
Use modern male CT segment corridors plus thoracic/rib level constraints to select final length; do not simply scale the old sternum stick.
Refit anterior rib/costal-cartilage contacts after sternum and thoracic spine are rebuilt.

SC_joint_implications.rule: Do not invent bilateral SC-centre breadth. Use the source table if obtained or an independently verified manubrial/clavicular-notch geometry.

acceptance_tests: jugular→xiphisternal geometry uses matching manubrium/body definitions and does not include xiphoid length
bilateral SC centres lie on reconstructed clavicular notches with explicit joint spaces
sternal angle and costal attachment levels remain compatible with the rebuilt thoracic spine/ribs
sternum remains one conventional adult bone; segment landmarks do not create extra bones
neutral shoulder and rib motion tests are rerun after SC/sternum changes
